closed.conclusion: openPilotCatalogFromVerifiedHandle and Snapshot now publish known operation failure to shared health before Unlock. Explicit mandatory health, post-lock recheck and constructor rejection remain intact. The new startup-sync and snapshot-read tests hold the failed operation inside Unlock after releasing its gate, proving a sibling rejects during the formerly unsafe window.

findings.detail: The child writes ready before calling Lock, and the parent interprets no acquired file for 150ms as exclusion. A descheduled child can make a no-op lock pass this check. This is timing evidence, not the named-barrier contention proof required by section 109. The final command.Wait is also unbounded; deferred Kill cannot run while Wait itself is stuck.
findings.required: Obtain an explicit child contention result while the parent still holds the same lock, for example a platform nonblocking exclusive-lock probe returning the expected contention class, followed by release and successful real blocking acquisition. Give process completion a bounded wait and owned kill/join cleanup before TempDir removal. Preserve actual child exit/error evidence.
findings.scope: Test acceptance blocker; not evidence that the platform lock implementation is broken.

limits: No additional code blocker found in the reviewed health or platform-lock changes.
Bootstrap/verified-handle/ACL, process-death lock release and full supervisor integration remain separate unproved gates.
